screenshot.identityReadback: The screenshot visibly identifies exact Area resref m2a_tlcdm4_ar and shows the detailed-material ship placeable.

toolset.observedProblem: The exact Toolset candidate is recognizable as the same ship silhouette, but the timber is a largely uniform brown result and does not match the light, differentiated Material Separation editor viewport.

sameSourceGeometry.conclusion: The candidate uses the exact canonical source hash and preserves all source triangles. The evidence rejects the hypothesis that a different source model was packaged.

facts: The demo loads source GLB, Material Separation JSON and texture-authoring metadata.
It does not load the referenced PNG texture payload bytes into the editor.
MaterialSeparationEditor resets textureFiles to an empty map for the loaded authoring document.
The viewport renders SourceViewport with faceMaterialOverlay colors taken from authored material previewColor.
The demo initializes world-scale UV selections as empty and does not load the frozen material-uv-projection document.
webPreviewBehavior.conclusion: The web editor image is a Material ID diagnostic overlay, not a renderer-parity preview of the exported MDL, TGA resources and projected UVs.

auroraCandidateBehavior.conclusion: Aurora renders the actual packaged TGA payloads and projected UVs rather than the editor's previewColor overlay.

diagnosis.proven: The application presented a diagnostic Material ID overlay as if it represented final authored textures. This preview/export parity defect explains the major visual mismatch.
diagnosis.notProven: The evidence does not establish an Aurora or NWN geometry-interpretation defect. A renderer-specific difference may still exist, but it must be tested only after the application renders the same texture payloads and UV projection as the export.
rejectedHypotheses: A different Meshy source model was packaged.
Aggressive geometry cleanup removed or substituted the ship geometry.

requiredNextSteps: Load and render exact texture payload bytes in the Material Separation viewport.
Load the exact material-uv-projection document and apply the same projected UVs used by the binary writer.
Add a converted binary-MDL readback viewport using the packaged texture resources.
Add a parity gate that prevents a previewColor diagnostic overlay from being presented as final texture appearance.
Only after parity is established compare the exact readback view with owner Toolset evidence and decide whether the material payload itself needs another candidate.
